rationale: Round-4 confirm at fix commit 7cc6421a (scoped exactly to internal/hook/hook.go + readstate_test.go, as claimed). (1) Both new internal/hook tests are real and green, run verbosely: TestReadState_BeadsDirPresent_DerivationFailure_ReturnsNonNil pins the exact reproduction fixture (.beads present, phase.SetListJSONForTest returning a genuine error, no session file) and asserts non-nil with Mode == state.ModeIndeterminate — and ModeIndeterminate is the pre-existing spec-128 sentinel in internal/state/state.go, not a new invention; TestPreCommit_BeadsDirPresent_DerivationFailure_BlocksOnProtectedBranch drives the REAL Run("pre-commit", &Input{}, ReadState, true) — real git repo via mustGitInit, real config.yaml with protected_branches:[main] and pre_commit_hook:true, the real ReadState (no injected stateFn) — and asserts Block, proving the hook DECISION, not just the return value. The full internal/hook package suite (32 tests, no -short skips) is green including every pre-existing dispatch/parse/emit test, so the synthetic-stateFn tests were not weakened. The hook.go diff matches the commit's nil-path audit: the DerivationFailed branch sets the honest ModeIndeterminate sentinel (never empty, never a fabricated phase), and the final nil-check is narrowed with !derivationFailed so post-initialization 'no state' is unreachable — the branch-protection bypass (outage read as 'not initialized, allow') is closed at both the value and decision layers. (2) Full `go test -short ./...`: my first run FAILED with internal/instruct panicking on go test's default 10m package timeout (601s) — investigated rather than hand-waved: internal/instruct has ZERO dependency on internal/hook (go list -deps confirms no import path, so 7cc6421a cannot influence it), the package passes alone in 152s with no single slow/hung test (worst individual test 4.9s; the ~150s is the sum of many 2-5s template/JSON tests), and a clean full-suite rerun is green: exit 0, 48 packages ok, zero FAIL. Conclusion: environmental load flake (this machine runs multiple panel reviewers concurrently), not a regression of this commit. Bead worktree left clean at 7cc6421a; /tmp scratch deleted.

findings.title: internal/instruct's -short wall time (~150s) leaves little headroom under go test's default 10m timeout on a loaded machine
findings.detail: The package intermittently times out when the host is under concurrent load (observed once this round: 'panic: test timed out after 10m0s', 601s; green alone at 152s and green on full-suite rerun). Not caused by 7cc6421a — internal/instruct has no import path to internal/hook — and the cost predates this round (many 2-5s git-fixture/template tests, e.g. TestRenderJSON_AllModes 4.9s). Worth a follow-up bead for fixture reuse or per-test parallelism in that package so CI/orchestrator runs don't flake; no change required in this bead.
